articles.title: Trump’s address kicks off jam-packed day at UNGA
articles.summary: In today’s issue: ▪ Trump at UN General Assembly ▪ White House press ban rages on ▪ Hung Cao’s bid for Navy Secretary ▪ Trump’s deal with Greenland and Denmark President Trump’s address to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Tuesday marks the beginning of a high-intensity day of meetings touching on major conflicts…
articles.body:
▪ Trump’s deal with Greenland and Denmark

President Trump ’s address to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Tuesday marks the beginning of a high-intensity day of meetings touching on major conflicts around the globe, including the war with Iran, U.S. control over Venezuela and a deal to end the intra-NATO fight over Greenland.

Trump will address the General Assembly around 9:55 a.m. EDT, and he is expected to berate past administrations for neglecting problems that he’s taken on in his second administration.

“He’ll include many of the issues, frankly neglected by past administrations, that he’s not going to kick the can on,” a senior administration official previewed last week in a call to reporters.

Trump will address the more than six-month war against Iran by touching “on the importance of ensuring that Iran never has a nuclear weapon,” discuss the president’s 20-point peace plan for Gaza — which has stalled for nearly a year — and the U.S. focus on the Western Hemisphere, the official previewed.

The president will almost surely mention some of the logistical issues during his UNGA appearance last year, when an escalator stopped on his way to the assembly and the teleprompter glitched during his speech — issues he’s framed in a somewhat conspiratorial light.

Following his speech, Trump will join a signing ceremony with the leaders of Greenland and Denmark on an agreement that the president touted as giving the U.S. “total control” over the Arctic island’s security. Greenland and Denmark, which owns the self-governed island, framed the agreement as strengthening security and said they will need to have their parliaments ratify the terms before it goes into effect.

The deal gives the U.S. permanent basing rights on the island, a provision already guaranteed by a 1951 treaty but that may have been in question if Greenland achieved independence. The agreement also bans sensitive investment on the island from countries outside of NATO.

After the signing, Trump will participate in three bilateral meetings. He’ll hold his first face-to-face with the recently appointed U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham and a “fulsome” bilateral with Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi . He’ll then meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky before taking part in a “Shield of the Americas” event with Latin American leaders.

A senior administration official described the Takaichi bilat as an important meeting coming the day before Trump welcomes Chinese President Xi Jinping for a state visit in Washington D.C. Top of Takaichi’s agenda is lobbying Trump not to trade economic deals with Beijing for Taiwan’s security.

Another high-stakes gathering is Trump’s meeting with Gulf countries to strategize on ending the war with Iran. Not expected to be part of that meeting is Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , who launched the war with the U.S. on Feb. 28. A senior administration official suggested scheduling issues prevent a meeting between Trump and Netanyahu. The two leaders last met on July 29.

Trump will host a “Leaders reception” on Tuesday evening, where he will meet for the first time face-to-face Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodr íguez . Trump granted Rodríguezpower to govern the country after launching an audacious operation to capture the country’s authoritarian leader Nicolás Maduro .

A senior administration official described their scheduled meeting as a “pull aside.” Despite treating the meeting informally, it carries huge weight. Trump’s praise for Rodríguez comes at the expense of alienating the political opposition and the administration’s promise of a transition to democracy.

Trump is expected to depart New York on Tuesday evening, and it’s not clear if his schedule will cross over with a small Iranian delegation that the State Department approved to come to the General Assembly.

“I won’t get ahead of the president or secretary’s final schedule,” a senior administration official responded when asked if Secretary of State Marco Rubio might also have a chance to meet with the Iranians.

Reuters : Trump eyes busy week of meetings as UN General Assembly gathers.

Plus : Join The Hill’s Ian Swanson , Amie Parnes and special guest Democratic strategist Garry South, who has advised California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D), for a special “Fight for 2028” live discussion at noon EDT on the latest in Democratic politics.

They’ll discuss the end of Newsom’s term as governor as he eyes the 2028 race and his recent interview where he shared his thoughts on former Vice President Kamala Harris . They will also touch on Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) and her latest moves.

A federal appeals court reinstated Missouri Republicans’ 7-1 House map to be used in time for the November elections, delivering a boost for several GOP candidates who wanted a more favorable midterm map.

Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) hosted an event Monday night , with “special guest” Former President Bush, to raise money for a new committee supporting Republican Senate candidates in Maine, Ohio, Alaska, Iowa, Michigan, New Hampshire and Minnesota, according to The New York Times . Not part of the event: Texas Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton.

Trump’s approval rating dipped to an all-time low in the latest Reuters/Ipsos, with the midterms only six weeks away .

Journalists listen as President Trump speaks during an event about healthcare in the Oval Office of the White House, Sept. 18, 2026, in Washington. (Jacquelyn Martin, Associated Press)

UNITED RESISTANCE : Trump’s stripping of White House media credentials for CNN, MS NOW and Politico has spurred a united counteraction among television networks. The four remaining members of the TV pool — CBS, ABC, NBC and Fox News — announced Monday they would not cover the president as long as the CNN remains banned.

But the White House shows no signs of backing down. The three banned media organizations filed lawsuits on Monday, and legal observers — along with the president — predict they will be successful.

In a joint statement, CNN, MS NOW and Politico said that they are taking legal action to “defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports.” A hearing for the case is slated for Wednesday afternoon.

Trump’s decision has drawn criticism from media organizations and Democrats, as well as some Trump supporters.

“I don’t disagree with the president’s concern about some of these outlets, I just think there’s more effective ways to do this,” Sean Spicer , Trump’s first-ever press secretary, told The Hill on Monday.

A White House official told The Hill that “Fake News has no place demanding a spot in the President’s Oval Office.”

“The lies they smear are a disservice to the American public and tear at the very fabric of our Democracy, ” the official said. “ They’re completely capable of reporting from directly outside.”

▪ BBC : CNN, MS NOW and Politico file lawsuit against Trump’s White House ban.

HARD TIMES : Iowa Republicans are leading the charge for federal action to tackle soaring diesel prices, as polls show alarming trends toward Democrats in the midterms.

“Iowans are being squeezed and shouldn’t have to foot the bill at the pump or the checkout line for the war in Iran. We need to use every option at our disposal to provide some relief from high prices,” Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa), the Republican candidate in Iowa’s Senate race, wrote on the social platform X.

She called to suspend gas taxes, pause exports on diesel and put in place a “diesel relief program to help our farmers and truckers being crushed by high costs.”

Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) Saturday night on X addressed the president directly, urging him to embargo diesel exports.

“High diesel prices ARE KILLING FARMERS INCOME,” Grassley wrote.

And Rep. Zach Nunn (R-Iowa), who’s running for reelection this November, responded to Grassley’s post with a plan of his own.

“Sell American energy to Americans first. Pass my Iowa-led biofuel bill = bring down gas 50 cents,” Nunn wrote on X. “Hold Big Oil accountable for gouging.”

A Marist poll out today shows Hinson trailing Democrat Josh Turek by 8 points in their race, and Republican gubernatorial candidate Zach Lahn trailing Democrat Rob Sand by 12 points. Hinson has held a slight lead in most recent polls.

PARAMOUNT SETTLEMENT : Paramount Skydance announced Monday that it was settling with the 12 states that sued the media giant in July over its proposed purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery.

“This includes more film production, protections for Hollywood workers and places guardrails that allow for robust cable negotiations and creates more choice,” California Attorney General Rob Bonta (D) told reporters at a press conference in Los Angeles. “This settlement is not a vote of support for this merger or a blessing.”

Bonta, who led the group of state attorneys general involved in the lawsuit, added, “We believe further consolidation in markets does not serve the American economy, consumers or competition well.”

The settlement follows months of contentious debate, with states claiming that the planned $100 billion merger violates antitrust laws.

“Our goal has always been to build a stronger Hollywood — one with more stories told, greater choice for consumers and stronger competition,” Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison said in a Monday statement.

Newsom called the deal “a win for California workers and our creative economy ” and praised Bonta’s efforts.

▪ The Hill : Paramount settles with 12 states over Warner Bros. Discovery merger.

▪ Reuters : Paramount wins Warner Bros takeover after settling states, union lawsuits.

TOGETHER AGAIN: Trump and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) met at Gracie Mansion Monday evening, where the president told reporters the mayor has “great potential” following their meeting.

“No, I certainly hope he will be a great mayor,” Trump said. “You have to understand — I want what’s good for New York. I want what’s good for the country.”

“So, if I had a choice of having him be a bad mayor or horrible mayor, I don’t want that,” he continued. “I want him to be a great mayor, and he’s certainly got potential and great potential.”

The two spoke about immigration, policing and affordable housing, per The New York Times. Mamdani emphasized that Trump’s lifting of temporary protected status for Haitian immigrants harmed New York City’s economy. The president acknowledged that the mayor felt “very strongly” about the issue but did not say if the administration would make any changes.

Trump has gone after Mamdani’s democratic socialist policies as the latter campaigned for his position last year. Although Trump has continued to criticize some of the mayor’s left-wing ideas, including his new proposed tax on second homes, this is the third time the president has had a cordial meeting with Mamdani.

▪ The Hill : Trump says Mamdani has ‘great potential’ after Gracie Mansion visit.

▪ The New York Times : Mamdani and Trump discuss immigration and affordability at Gracie Mansion.

Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao testifies at a House Appropriations subcommittee on the budget request for the Navy and Marine Corps on Capitol Hill, May 12, 2026, in Washington. (Mariam Zuhaib, Associated Press)

CONCERNS ABOUT CAO : The fight to confirm Hung Cao as Navy secretary won’t be easy, with Democrats already throwing up roadblocks.

Cao, who currently heads the Navy in a temporary capacity, filled the role in April, following the departure of former secretary John Phelan . The president nominated Cao for the full-time position on Sept. 1.

But The Hill’s Ellen Mitchell reports that Democrats have major concerns about Cao’s history leading the Navy — and they have leverage, as the retired Navy captain requires a waiver. Cao retired in 2021, and federal law requires a seven-year wait for some top civilian posts.

“Hung Cao has shown he has neither the ability nor the temperament to serve as Navy Secretary,” Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.) said in a statement to The Hill.

Democratic senators are particularly worried about Cao’s management of the USS Abraham Lincoln’s long and controversial deployment.

“Given Acting Secretary Cao’s lack of leadership in addressing the concerns raised regarding the extended deployment of the USS Abraham Lincoln and his focus on advancing [Defense] Secretary [Pete] Hegseth ’s ideological war on DEI [diversity, equity and inclusion], I have concerns about Mr. Cao’s ability to preserve the integrity and safety of the Navy,” Sen. Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii) said in a statement to The Hill.

Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.) also emphasized the conditions aboard the naval ship, calling Cao’s leadership a “severe mishandling.”

Even if Senate Republicans do press ahead with Cao’s confirmation process, it’s unlikely to happen anytime soon, with Senate leaders carefully managing floor time in their two remaining work weeks before the midterms, Mitchell writes.

▪ The Hill : Hung Cao’s bid for Navy secretary faces choppy waters post-USS Abraham Lincoln.

An iceberg is visible near the city of Ilulissat, Greenland, Feb. 19, 2025. (Emilio Morenatti, Associated Press file)

DAMAGE DONE : Trump last week announced a deal with Greenland and Denmark that expands the U.S.’s military presence and gives a bigger say in the Arctic island’s affairs. The deal brings relief to fellow NATO members, but the fight will leave scars, The Hill’s Laura Kelly and Filip Timotija report .

Trump is to meet with Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenland’s Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen for a signing ceremony in New York on Tuesday morning.

“The icy outpost is valuable strategic territory, though it’s fair to ask whether this deal could have been reached without the collateral damage to U.S. alliances from Mr. Trump’s bullying threats,” The Wall Street Journal’s editorial board wrote Sunday.

Mike Waltz , Trump’s ambassador to the U.N., shared the opinion story to highlight the deal.

“Securing our Northern flank. Permanent U.S. basing rights in Greenland keep our homeland safe, deny adversary access, and reinforce American peace through strength leadership on the global stage,” he wrote on the social platform X .

Baiba Braže , Latvian foreign minister and a NATO ally, told The Hill in a Saturday interview, “ Let’s wait until the deal is signed ,” when asked for her reaction. She described negotiations as “tense.”

The deal is “ unlikely to quiet concerns European allies have over America’s broader commitment to the Allianc e,” said Torrey Taussig , director of the Transatlantic Security Initiative at the Atlantic Council. But she said it also shows how European leaders can work to ensure cooler heads prevail.

Michael McFaul , a prominent Trump critic and former U.S. ambassador to Russia during the Obama administration, said on X that the agreement is a “slight tweak” to what has already been in place.

“Trump did not buy or annex Greenland. He just repackaged an old agreement and put his name on it,” he wrote Sunday.

Trump’s Achilles heel is the stock market, Joslin Joseph writes in The Hill.

America is blundering toward war with China, Robert D. Kaplan writes in The New York Times.

Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker speaks at a Texas Democratic Party press conference ahead of the Republican National Convention, Sept. 9, 2026, in Dallas. (Gabriela Passos, Associated Press)

And finally … Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker (D) lost 80 pounds using a GLP-1 drug.

“I have been driven my whole life to lose weight,” Pritzker said in a Monday episode of “CBS Mornings.”

The governor, whose father died at age 39 from a heart attack, said he decided to try a GLP-1 following a diabetes diagnosis two years ago. Since then, he’s felt “a whole lot different and a whole lot better.”

When asked if his decision to lose weight was tied to a potential 2028 presidential run, Pritzker insisted that he was focused on his role as governor and touted that Illinois’s state insurance plan covers GLP-1 medications for its 55,000 state employees.

“I have an opportunity just with the platform that I have as governor to tell people that this is something that can work for them,” Pritzker said.

articles.title: Trump administration to remove 760,000 Affordable Care Act enrollees over fraud claims
articles.summary: Vice President JD Vance and other Trump administration officials said Tuesday they plan to remove 760,000 Affordable Care Act enrollees from public healthcar...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Vice President JD Vance and other Trump administration officials said Tuesday they plan to remove 760,000 Affordable Care Act enrollees from public healthcare exchanges, alleging that the individuals were fraudulently enrolled in the program, or simply do not exist.

Vance said the discovery and canceled subsidy payments for hundreds of thousands of people from the exchanges, part of an administration-wide crackdown on fraud , would result in $2.2 billion in cost savings.

"We're actually making sure that the people receiving Obamacare subsidies are actually entitled to receive them," said Vance, who leads a government task force to eliminate fraud. He was flanked by Dr. Mehmet Oz, the administrator for the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, or CMS, and other administration officials.

Vance said the cancellation of approximately 315,000 enrollments covering 760,000 people was done in part because the government was not checking whether people enrolled were eligible. Vance said another 419,000 enrollments will get additional verification to make sure they are eligible for the benefit.

The Trump administration also announced a six-month suspension on new agents or brokers who sign up enrollees for healthcare coverage, who officials say commit a disproportionate amount of the fraud they uncovered.

Roughly 19.2 million Americans are actively enrolled in ACA marketplace health plans as of early 2026, according to the Department of Health and Human Services website. The number of enrollees grew during the COVID-19 pandemic when enhanced subsidies became available through the American Rescue Plan Act and Inflation Reduction Act, both signed into law by former President Joe Biden.

Tuesday's announcement is the latest in an initiative by the Trump administration to address fraud around the country, including in federal healthcare programs, which officials say is needed to rein in runaway spending and protect taxpayers.

Some healthcare policy experts are calling for more transparency on how the Trump administration decided to cut hundreds of thousands of enrollees — and question how many people may have been wrongly cut from the program.

Cynthia Cox, a vice president and director of the ACA program at the healthcare research nonprofit KFF, said "I think there's no question that somebody who was fraudulently enrolled should have their coverage canceled," however, "I think the question is whether this was the appropriate process by which to identify fraudulent enrollees, and also whether all of them were indeed fraudulently enrolled."

Cox said the elimination of the people from ACA programs was done outside of the normal regulatory process.

Ellen Montz, a former deputy administrator and director at the Center for Consumer Information and Insurance Oversight at CMS during the Biden administration said during her time in government, there was an ongoing effort to eliminate fraud from ACA programs.

"There's a lot of work to be done, and the Trump administration has done some good things that are targeting the actual fraudsters," she said. Adding that Tuesday's announcement lacked details on how the administration determined who to cut. " I would imagine we'll hear from some subset of consumers that ask: why did my enrollment get cancelled?" Montz said.

At the press conference, Tuesday, Vance referred to some enrollments lacking social security numbers or immigration documentation.

The announcement comes as stubbornly high inflation and rising healthcare costs pressure the Trump administration to come up with a plan to bring down costs for Americans as affordability remains a central issue in the fall midterm elections.

The price of ACA insurance has skyrocketed for many Americans during Trump's second term, after Republicans opposed extending COVID-era subsidies that had helped offset the costs of health insurance for most enrollees during Biden's term.

Premiums doubled or tripled for many enrollees, prompting millions to downgrade their plans or exit the program entirely after the Republican-led Congress allowed the subsidies to expire this year.

The Government Accountability Office suggests fraud risks in the advance premium tax credit do exist - however it's unclear at what scale. The GAO conducted covert testing using fictitious ACA applicants enrolled in 2024 and 2025. A report released in December showed that the federal marketplace approved subsidized coverage for almost all of the GAO's 24 fake enrollees.

The White House referred The Associated Press to the Vice President's team for additional comment on bigger plans to address healthcare affordability. The Vice President's office and CMS did not respond to Associated Press requests for comment.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the news of the Trump administration's plan to remove ACA enrollees from public exchanges.

Democratic lawmakers criticized the move to remove enrollees from ACA coverage.

Richard E. Neal, a Massachusetts Democrat and ranking member of the Ways and Means Committee, said "Republicans have already created the worst healthcare crisis ever, but every decision by the Trump Administration is designed to keep making it worse."

"As if making coverage harder to access through skyrocketing premiums and more red tape wasn't painful enough, they're doubling down to take it away entirely," Neal said.

articles.title: Postal worker threw out 300 mail-in ballots out of self-described ‘laziness,’ DOJ says
articles.summary: Postal worker threw out 300 mail-in ballots out of self-described ‘laziness,’ DOJ says
articles.body:
WASHINGTON — An overwhelmed U.S. postal worker in Utah threw 300 mail-in ballots into a parking lot dumpster shortly before the state's June 23 primary election in which both Democrats and Republicans were on the ballot, Justice Department officials said Tuesday.

The 34-year-old mail carrier told investigators that he did not have a political agenda and that he tossed other mail when he ditched the ballots, Melissa Holyoak, U.S. attorney for the District of Utah, said. She said roughly 95% of voters do so by mail in the state, and it wasn't clear yet whether they were able to eventually cast ballots.

According to a government memo , Damon Matai Seei told investigators that he wanted to toss out advertisements to "lighten his workload" after feeling overwhelmed.

"He claims he simply made a 'poor decision' out of 'frustration' and 'laziness,'" the memo said. He didn't intend to toss any ballots, they said. Seei is no longer with the U.S. Postal Service. He pleaded not guilty Tuesday to a charge of destruction and delay of mail.

The U.S. Postal Service said in a statement that it works "tirelessly to ensure public trust in the mail and monitors to prevent any issues that may arise," and that it closely monitors political and election mail.

The agency said it was notified of a mail dumping, and referred the matter to the inspector general, "specifically charged with investigating alleged crimes" by postal service employees.

"The unique status of political and election mail makes its security a top priority during every election cycle," according to the statement, and works to "to prevent, identify and resolve any issues that might interfere with its secure and timely delivery."

Justice Department officials held a news conference in Washington to announce the charge as part of its efforts to promote "election integrity." Federal prosecutors have made possible voter fraud — which is rare — a priority, as President Donald Trump insists without evidence that noncitizens are voting en masse and has sought to limit mail-in ballots. The Supreme Court last week refused to allow the president's mail-in restrictions to be enforced.

Trump has repeatedly made false claims that he won the 2020 election and has falsely claimed he won the popular vote in 2016, yet the Trump administration has struggled during both terms to bring cases showing evidence of significant voter fraud . That's despite a massive effort in Trump's second term to obtain voter registration records from states in an attempt to determine if there were any noncitizens registered.

So far during the president's second term, the Justice Department has charged 70 voter-fraud-related cases, officials said Tuesday. More than 170 million people are registered to vote in the U.S.

Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter said there were more cases in the works, but he didn't provide further details or a timeline.

"Under the leadership of President Trump and Attorney General Blanche, this department is committed to protecting the vote of American citizens," he said.

The Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, meanwhile, is revving up a long-standing election monitoring program but putting a new emphasis on "ballot security" and staffing the effort with newly hired conservative personnel who have replaced longtime career employees, hundreds of whom have departed en masse since Trump returned to office. The Civil Rights Division's efforts to seize voter rolls have resulted in a string of court losses — with 25 courts ruling against the federal government.

Voting rights experts say isolated instances of fraud do happen, as do issues with voting machines, but not on a scale that could have changed the outcome of the 2020 presidential election, which was won by Democrat Joe Biden .

But the materials that the Justice Department releases could help feed Trump's broader narrative about elections. And with the majority of voters disapproving of Trump's presidency and saying his policies have hurt the economy , Republicans are facing a tough midterms picture.

Earlier this month, the Justice Department rolled out five voting-related cases , four of which were brought against noncitizens. Last week, the Justice Department announced that 16 individuals had been charged in election-related cases, with a news release mentioning that at least 10 of them were lawful permanent residents of the United States. The defendants were originally from Mexico, Nigeria, India, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Antigua and Barbuda, Venezuela, and Colombia.

There was also a defendant from Russia: Victoria Aquilina, a 42-year-old Russian national who entered the United States as an au pair in her early 20s, was charged with casting a ballot in the 2024 election.

Trump — who, until he won the 2024 election, faced federal criminal charges over his efforts to overturn his 2020 loss in the lead-up to the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol — said earlier this year that Republicans should " nationalize the voting ."

Democrats, meanwhile, have launched an "unprecedented" effort to combat potential disruption of the 2026 midterm elections.

Seei's next court date is Nov. 30. His federal public defender did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: House Republicans drop Jack Smith transcripts in explosive Arctic Frost records fight
articles.summary: House Republicans released transcripts from Jack Smith's team, alleging improper subpoenas targeted GOP lawmakers' phone records in the Arctic Frost probe.
articles.body:
House Republicans released transcripts revealing details of the investigation into President Trump and GOP lawmakers, including allegations of improper subpoenaing of phone records and gag orders on lawmakers.

Testimony from members of the special prosecutor's office shed light on the decision-making process and investigative techniques used in the Arctic Frost probe.

The transcripts also highlighted the unique characteristics of the investigation, such as the hands-on approach of former Special Counsel Jack Smith and the challenges of obtaining lawmakers' phone records.

House Republicans released six closely watched transcripts Tuesday, offering a new-look inside former Special Counsel Jack Smith's controversial investigation of President Donald Trump and Republican lawmakers.

Committee Republicans allege investigators improperly subpoenaed phone records belonging to more than a dozen GOP lawmakers during the Arctic Frost probe, and secured gag orders preventing lawmakers from learning the Biden-Harris Justice Department had obtained their records.

Taken together, they add substantial detail about the reasoning behind investigatory decisions — especially concerning how they approached probing lawmaker communications — as they investigated whether Trump had attempted to block the peaceful transfer of power after the 2020 election. They reveal efforts that Smith's office took to make sure the investigation followed the norms and processes that would apply to any investigation. But it also laid bare key differences in the way the investigation was practically carried out that separated it from most probes.

The documents include testimony from five members of the special prosecutor's office, including J.P. Cooney, Molly Gaston, Ray Hulser, Tad Duree and Thomas Windom, all members of Smith's team. The released files also include testimony from Brian Burnett, an agent for the Office of Inspector General (OIG).

The new revelations focus especially on communications gathered from Rep. Scott Perry, R-Pa., the only lawmaker who had his phone seized as a part of the investigation.

According to testimony from Smith's prosecutor, Timothy "Tad" Duree, investigators had decided to seize the phone using a warrant because of his proximity to Trump and his hand in trying to find a legal strategy to keep Trump in office after he lost. Notably, Perry was a go-between from Trump to Jeffrey Clark, the highest-ranking DOJ official willing to explore weaknesses in the 2020 election.

Duree described that warrant process as comparable to other investigations.

"If you seek to obtain something voluntarily, people can just choose not to give it to you. That's one obvious thing. But there are myriad opportunities for evidence to be altered, tampered with, deleted, added to. And in this search warrant, same as any others, it was important to me and our team to obtain evidence in a way that it was unadulterated," Duree said in his testimony.

The operation entailed pinging Perry's phone to find its location.

Thomas Windom testified investigators obtained a "location-warrant" — which found Perry to be on vacation in New Jersey. According to Duree's transcript, agents located Perry, seized his phone and imaged it, then returned it.

"In this particular case … the whole team wanted to image the phone and get it back to Congressman Perry as quickly as possible. We were trying real hard to do this in a way that was minimally disruptive, it was as respectful as it could be, and it didn't put Congressman Perry in an awkward spot where we're seizing a phone right out on Independence [Avenue] in front of the Rayburn Building or it's some big hubbub," Windom recalled.

More broadly, investigators also reassured lawmakers that Smith had been cautious about subpoenaing communications from members of Congress. Husler, another one of the prosecutors on Smith's team, said that they had looked to narrow the scope of which ones were deemed necessary.

"Well, I talked with him about it," Husler recalled about the selection process. "And, as we got into the May subpoenas, you could see, not only was it [a] narrow list of people, but there were written justifications for it. So he wanted to be very careful if we were going to be getting subpoenas for members."

Naturally, securing the communications of lawmakers came with complications.

Duree acknowledged that court-ordered secrecy surrounding subpoenas for lawmakers' phone records often prevented the lawmakers from challenging the demands while the orders were active. Duree said he did not particularly remember specifics from correspondence about obtaining Rep. Chip Roy's, R-Texas, phone records that were raised during his interview with investigators.

Rather than serving the subpoena on Roy, investigators sought the records from his phone provider. A nondisclosure order (NDO) prevented the provider from notifying the subscriber about the government's demand, essentially preventing the lawmaker from asking questions.

Duree acknowledged the practical limitation. A nondisclosure order "will prohibit a person who holds that phone number from litigating issues surrounding the subpoena," he testified.

He was then pressed as to whether he believed the act violated the Speech or Debate Clause of the Constitution that protects lawmakers.

Duree did not concede that obtaining the lawmakers' toll records violated the Speech or Debate Clause. Later in his testimony, he maintained that prosecutors believed the records they sought were not protected by the clause, while acknowledging there was a "lack of clarity on certain points" of the law that arose during the investigation.

"I would say we were hypervigilant and extremely aware of the contours of the Speech or Debate Clause. We knew that Speech or Debate was something that we had to navigate. We treated it seriously," he said, adding that while case law on the clause can appear "underdeveloped," he took it seriously.

"[It's] a common thing, particularly in complex investigations, to run into the corners of the law that aren't fully built out," he said.

While parts of the testimony underscored efforts to manage the investigation by the book, other parts highlighted some unusual characteristics.

The Justice Department's Public Integrity Section knew investigators were seeking Jordan's phone records when it approved the investigative step in April 2022, according to page seven of the transcript of Jack Smith team prosecutor Tad Duree. However, the OIG agent who served the subpoena to Verizon – Brain Burnett – did not know who the particular number belonged to, and only purportedly figured it out much later.

"It was not until I had been retired and this was on the news and there was conversation about Mr. Jordan's toll records being subpoenaed and then there was a subpoena that came up on the internet," Burnett testified, according to his own transcript.

"But I do not know, as we sit here today, if that was his number or not."

He said that if he had known just who the toll records belonged to, he would have raised the issue with his superiors. Burnett said that the records sought by "AUSAs" – federal prosecutors--were typically nameless: "Just phone numbers," he said.

The testimony illustrates a gap in the process – in that the DOJ's Public Integrity Section knew a particular phone number sought belonged to Jordan, while that information was not disclosed to subordinates.

Transcript testimony also revealed that Smith's work was more hands-on than other investigations.

A veteran agent assigned to the Jeffrey Clark investigation testified that the probe operated in a way "unique, as far as the over 30 years of law enforcement experience I have," according to transcript documents released by Jordan's panel.

Prosecutors directed investigative steps normally handled by agents, he said, describing the dynamic as "top down," in that when a forensics agent receives the results of a subpoena, it would go back to the prosecutor – not the agent who subpoenaed the records, according to Brian Burnett – one of six individuals whose interviews were released.

Burnett spent 15 years in the DOJ's inspector general's office before his 2024 retirement, and was a senior narcotics detective with the Chesterfield County Sheriff's office in a Richmond, Virginia suburb for nine years.

Asked whether he had encountered another case during his career in which prosecutors dictated the investigation in that manner, Burnett responded, "Not in my entire 30 years of law enforcement."

articles.title: CPI do Master: Zanin nega pedido para instalação no Senado | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministro afirmou que não ficou comprovada omissão da Presidência do Senado na análise dos requerimentos relacionados ao caso.
articles.summary: O ministro Cristiano Zanin negou determinar a instalação da CPI do Master por não identificar omissão ilegal da Presidência do Senado na análise dos requerimentos.
articles.body:
O ministro do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) Cristiano Zanin negou um pedido de liminar (decisão provisória) para determinar a instalação da CPI do Master no Senado . O pedido foi apresentado pelo senador Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE).

Zanin entendeu que não ficou devidamente comprovada uma omissão do presidente do Senado em relação à instalação da comissão.

Segundo o ministro, o pedido não esclareceu como ocorreu a tramitação nem qual foi a atuação da Presidência do Senado diante de um conjunto de requerimentos relacionados ao caso Master.

Zanin durante julgamento dos acusados de mandar matar Marielle Franco — Foto: Gustavo Moreno/STF

Zanin destacou ainda que o próprio senador reconheceu a existência de um requerimento anterior para a criação da CPI.

Para o ministro, essas informações são necessárias para avaliar se houve, de fato, uma omissão ilegal que justificasse a intervenção do Judiciário para determinar a instalação da comissão.

O senador Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) criticou a decisão e afirmou que apresentará novas informações ao STF para tentar garantir a instalação da CPI do Banco Master. O parlamentar disse que a decisão não encerra a discussão e afirmou que a omissão do Senado em instalar a CPI é "fato notório".

A defesa da instalação de Comissões Parlamentares de Inquérito (CPIs) para investigar o Banco Master está no centro da disputa política e de narrativa no Congresso entre o governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e a oposição bolsonarista.

Às vésperas da eleição, o cenário se intensificou após a crise no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF). Os embates entre ministros Alexandre de Moraes e André Mendonça começaram após a revelação do envio de pelo menos 52 mensagens de Vorcaro para Moraes.

Enquanto no Supremo a questão está paralisada após a suspensão dos julgamentos que iam analisar o relatório que cita Moraes e o pedido de investigação contra Mendonça, no Legislativo deputados e senadores querem explorar o tema politicamente.

No entanto, a cúpula do Congresso é contra a instalação de um colegiado para investigar o escândalo do banco de Daniel Vorcaro e, diante desse cenário, governistas e oposicionistas utilizam o tema de olho nas eleições deste ano.

Ao todo, o Congresso conta com sete iniciativas diferentes para criar comissões destinadas a investigar o Banco Master.

🔎 Para que uma Comissão Parlamentar de Inquérito seja criada, é necessário o apoio mínimo de um terço dos integrantes da respectiva Casa Legislativa. Para a Comissão ser instalada, é preciso que o requerimento seja lido em uma sessão.

✏️Além do número mínimo de assinaturas, o requerimento precisa indicar um fato determinado a ser investigado e estabelecer prazo certo para funcionamento da comissão.

Na Câmara dos Deputados, uma CPI depende da assinatura de ao menos 171 deputados.

No Senado, são necessárias 27 assinaturas de senadores.

Já uma CPMI — comissão mista formada por deputados e senadores — exige simultaneamente os dois quóruns: 171 deputados e 27 senadores.

articles.title: Crise no STF domina campanha e escanteia propostas | G1
articles.standfirst: Campanha de Lula avalia que Flávio Bolsonaro pode obter ganhos eleitorais com a crise; uma ala defende que o presidente se afaste do desgaste e cobre investigações de forma mais enfática.
articles.summary: Impasse no Supremo ocupa o centro da disputa eleitoral, dificulta estratégia de Lula e abre espaço para exploração política por Flávio Bolsonaro.
articles.body:
A crise no Supremo Tribunal Federal tomou o centro da campanha eleitoral e esvaziou o espaço para a discussão de propostas. Sem um desfecho, o desgaste do tribunal se prolonga e interfere nas estratégias dos candidatos à Presidência.

Na própria campanha do presidente Lula , a avaliação é que Flávio Bolsonaro consegue explorar politicamente esse cenário e obter dividendos eleitorais enquanto o Supremo permanecer como foco da disputa.

A preocupação ajuda a explicar a defesa enfática, feita por uma ala da campanha, de que Lula se afaste cada vez mais da crise. Para esse grupo, o presidente precisa ir além das declarações de que todos devem ser investigados e cobrar a apuração de forma mais contundente.

Embora vários ministros sejam citados e tenham explicações a dar, a avaliação é que o desgaste está muito concentrado na figura de Alexandre de Moraes .

A crise também atravessa uma estratégia que a campanha de Lula vinha tentando consolidar: fazer da soberania o assunto central da eleição.

A participação do presidente na Assembleia Geral da ONU, em Nova York, já estava prevista na agenda. A campanha, porém, busca transformar o evento em um ativo eleitoral, aproveitando o discurso e a exposição internacional para reforçar a imagem de Lula como estadista.

O material produzido durante a viagem pode abastecer a campanha e dar destaque a essa mensagem. No retorno ao Brasil, no entanto, o presidente volta a se deparar com uma crise no Supremo que continua sem solução e ocupa o debate político.

Do outro lado, Flávio Bolsonaro tenta manter o desgaste do tribunal no centro da campanha. A estratégia busca atingir ministros vistos como mais próximos de Lula, entre eles Moraes.

Isso ocorre apesar de o próprio Flávio ainda não ter esclarecido o pedido de dinheiro feito a Daniel Vorcaro para o que seria a produção de um filme sobre o pai, Jair Bolsonaro. Moraes também tem explicações a dar sobre contratos e relações com Vorcaro.

A permanência dessas questões sem esclarecimento alimenta a disputa eleitoral. Para a campanha de Lula, o risco é que o adversário continue capitalizando o desgaste do Supremo enquanto o presidente encontra dificuldade para impor os temas que gostaria de discutir.

O adiamento de uma solução para a crise, portanto, não fica restrito ao tribunal: repercute na eleição e mantém as propostas para o país em segundo plano.

articles.title: Brasil, União Europeia e outros países defendem soberania e criticam ameaças e uso da força | G1
articles.standfirst: Comunicado foi divulgado no contexto da Assembleia Geral da ONU. Nesta terça, Lula discursou e defendeu soberania do Brasil, afirmando que país não cabe no 'quintal' de ninguém.
articles.summary: Comunicado foi divulgado no contexto da Assembleia Geral da ONU. Nesta terça, Lula discursou e defendeu soberania do Brasil, afirmando que país não cabe no 'quintal' de ninguém.
articles.body:
Na ONU, Lula trata de soberania e critica interferências externas em processos eleitorais — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O grupo Parceiros pelo Multilateralismo , do qual o Brasil faz parte, emitiu um comunicado à comunidade internacional no qual defendeu a soberania dos países e a integridade territorial e se manifestou de forma contrária sobre ameaças e uso da força entre países.

Além do Brasil, integram o grupo a União Europeia , o Canadá, a Índia e a Austrália, além de outros países.

Nesta terça, ao discursar na assembleia da ONU, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) defendeu a soberania do Brasil e o processo eleitoral.

Ele acresscentou que o país não cabe no “quintal” de ninguém, em uma referência a ações americanas na região que o governo considera como tentativas de interferência no processo eleitoral.

“Sustentamos a necessidade de defender e fazer cumprir as normas, os princípios e os compromissos que seguem essenciais à ordem internacional e, ao mesmo tempo, renovar e reformar o sistema multilateral, de modo a torná-lo mais eficaz, representativo, inclusivo e adequado a seus propósitos", diz o documento do grupo.

O texto prossegue: "Reafirmamos nosso compromisso com o direito internacional e com os princípios da igualdade soberana, da integridade territorial, da solução pacífica de controvérsias e da proibição da ameaça ou do uso da força".

Conforme auxiliares de Lula, ao fazer menção à soberania brasileira no discurso na ONU, sem citar o nome do presidente Donald Trump, o petista conseguiu dar um recado à comunidade internacional de que não aceitará ingerência externa no processo eleitoral, classificado por Lula como “moderno e robusto”.

Entre outros pontos, o governo brasileiro vê como tentativas de ingerência americana:

a classificação do PCC e do Comando Vermelho como organizações terroristas;

a indicação de um político de direita, e não de um diplomata, para o cargo de embaixador no Brasil.

Para além do cenário no Brasil, diplomatas dizem que ações americanas na região também têm representado violação da soberania interna dos países, como:

ação militar americana em Caracas que resultou na prisão do então presidente da Venezuela Nicolás Maduro;

ação militar aérea americana que atingiu embarcações na costa da Colômbia;

declarações de Trump de que Cuba “é a próxima” quando questionado sobre ações militares americanas no Irã.

Em outro trecho do comunicado, o grupo internacional afirma defender o chamado multilateralismo porque é “indispensável” perseguir os princípios da ONU, entre os quais a paz, a descolonização e a dignidade, num cenário em que causa preocupação a “crescente polarização”.

O grupo acrescenta, então, que é necessário os países cumprirem o direito internacional — diversos países têm criticado o governo de Israel nesse sentido, afirmando que a gestão de Benjamin Netanyahu fere os princípios internacionais em suas ações militares em Gaza.

“Nos preocupam a crescente polarização, a disseminação de conflitos, as violações do direito internacional e o recurso cada vez mais frequente à política do poder, ao protecionismo, à coerção e à ameaça ou ao uso da força", afirma o grupo.

"Essas tendências representam ameaça à paz e à segurança internacionais e prejudicam a cooperação global precisamente no momento em que ela se faz mais necessária do que nunca”, conclui o texto.

articles.title: Contarato quer banir bets e mais tempo de internação para menores | G1
articles.standfirst: As propostas do candidato ao Senado pelo Espírito Santo foram apresentadas durante entrevista ao vivo ao Bom Dia Espírito Santo nesta quarta-feira (23).
articles.summary: As propostas do candidato ao Senado pelo Espírito Santo foram apresentadas durante entrevista ao vivo ao Bom Dia Espírito Santo nesta quarta-feira (23).
articles.body:
O candidato ao Senado pelo Espírito Santo, Fabiano Contarato (PT), defendeu, durante entrevista ao vivo ao Bom Dia Espírito Santo nesta quarta-feira (23), o aumento do tempo de internação para adolescentes que cometem crimes graves, a proibição das apostas esportivas on-line, as chamadas bets, e o fim da escala de trabalho 6x1 sem redução de salário.

Ao falar sobre a jornada, ele comparou a situação de trabalhadores que recebem salário mínimo e trabalham seis dias por semana à ' condição análoga à escravidão'.

"Costumo falar que você numa escala 6 por 1, ganhando R$ 1.621, é um crime de redução à condição análoga do escravo. Eu falei isso dentro do Senado. Eu queria ver se fossem nós, parlamentares, ganhando R$ 1.621, numa escala 6 por 1, não tendo tempo para você estar com seu filho, com sua filha, não tendo tempo para você se divertir ou estar com quem você ama", disse.

Contarato defendeu a redução da maioridade penal para 16 anos, mas reconhece que a mudança esbarra na Constituição. O artigo 228 estabelece que menores de 18 anos são penalmente inimputáveis, e o senador considera que essa regra não poderia ser alterada por uma mudança comum na legislação.

Como alternativa, ele apresentou um projeto para aumentar o tempo máximo de internação de adolescentes que cometem atos infracionais.

A proposta prevê ampliar o limite de três para cinco anos e, nos casos de atos cometidos com violência, grave ameaça ou equivalentes a crimes hediondos, permitir internação de até dez anos. O projeto foi aprovado no Senado e enviado para análise da Câmara dos Deputados.

“Eu aumentei o período de internação, que hoje é de três anos, passando para cinco. E se for praticado com violência, grave ameaça, hediondo, pode chegar a dez anos de internação”, disse.

Contarato citou como exemplo o ataque a uma escola em Aracruz, no Espírito Santo, e afirmou que, pela proposta dele, o adolescente responsável poderia ter permanecido internado por até dez anos.

Fabiano Contarato participou de entrevista ao vivo no Bom Dia Espírito Santo — Foto: Reprodução TV Gazeta

No pingue-pongue do início da entrevista, Contarato respondeu que é favorável ao fim das bets. Ao desenvolver o tema, afirmou que, se dependesse dele, as plataformas de apostas on-line seriam banidas.

"Se dependesse de mim, Fabiano Contarato , eu baniria as bets", afirmou.

Segundo o candidato, o principal problema está nos impactos das apostas sobre as famílias e, principalmente, sobre os jovens. Ele também defendeu como alternativa o aumento da tributação das plataformas.

Contarato defendeu o fim da escala 6x1 sem redução de salário. Questionado sobre o impacto da mudança para pequenos empresários, disse que o governo poderia criar incentivos fiscais para ajudar as empresas.

“É óbvio que se você tiver que fazer algum ajuste para dar um incentivo fiscal para que as empresas se adequem, isso não tem problema. Vamos fazer isso”, afirmou.

Trabalhadores pedem fim da escala 6x1 em ato realizado em Belo Horizonte — Foto: TV Globo/ Reprodução

Ao defender a mudança, o candidato comparou a situação de trabalhadores que recebem salário mínimo e trabalham seis dias por semana à "condição análoga à escravidão".

"Você numa escala 6 por 1 ganhando R$ 1.621 é um crime de redução à condição análoga do escravo", disse.

Ao falar sobre segurança pública, Contarato se posicionou contra a classificação de facções criminosas como organizações terroristas. Para ele, o Brasil já possui instituições capazes de combater o crime e a adoção desse rótulo poderia gerar consequências no âmbito internacional.

“Eu não concordo, porque você está declarando para o mundo que as suas instituições são incompetentes. E eu tenho muito orgulho das instituições que compõem a segurança pública. Sou contra rotular, porque quando você assim faz, você impacta no chamado direito internacional, e isso abre um precedente para que outros países possam querer intervir aqui”, afirmou.

O candidato defendeu investimentos em inteligência, tecnologia e compartilhamento de informações entre União, estados e municípios.

Contarato defendeu mudanças nas regras para escolha e permanência dos ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal. Entre as propostas citadas estão mandato de dez anos, idade mínima maior e escolha a partir de uma lista tríplice.

Ele também defendeu transparência na declaração de bens dos ministros e em valores recebidos por palestras ou outras atividades relacionadas ao cargo.

Questionado sobre um eventual processo de impeachment do ministro Alexandre de Moraes, Contarato afirmou que, considerando as informações que tinha no momento da entrevista, votaria favoravelmente à abertura do processo.

O candidato também defendeu uma regulamentação mais rígida das grandes plataformas digitais. Contarato citou o chamado PL das Fake News e afirmou que a proposta estabelece regras para plataformas com mais de 40 milhões de acessos por mês.

Segundo o candidato, a regulamentação não teria como objetivo retirar o direito à liberdade de expressão, mas responsabilizar plataformas e usuários pela prática de crimes.

Durante a entrevista, ele citou episódios relacionados à sua vida pessoal e à família para argumentar que a liberdade de expressão não deve servir de proteção para conteúdos que, segundo ele, ultrapassem os limites legais.

Contarato também mencionou ataques relacionados à sua vida pessoal, incluindo referências à sua orientação sexual, aos filhos, à adoção e à cor da pele. Para ele, as plataformas precisam ter responsabilidade sobre o conteúdo publicado e mecanismos para impedir que as redes sejam usadas para cometer crimes.

“Eu sou favorável, porque se sua liberdade de expressão, ela fere, machuca, dói ou mata, você tem que ter responsabilidade”, afirmou.

Contarato criticou os chamados penduricalhos e defendeu o cumprimento do teto constitucional no serviço público. "Teto é teto", afirmou.

Ele comparou os valores recebidos por parte de servidores públicos aos salários de trabalhadores que recebem o mínimo e trabalham na escala 6x1.

O candidato também criticou a existência de verbas que ultrapassariam o teto constitucional. “Eu não acho razoável você falar que o teto de um funcionário público é R$ 47 mil, mas alguns funcionários públicos podem chegar hoje [...] a R$ 80 mil”, disse.

Sobre o combate à violência contra a mulher, Contarato afirmou que o aumento das penas não é suficiente para enfrentar o problema. “Esse comportamento passa também por uma questão socioeconômica e cultural”, afirmou.

Ele defendeu ações de prevenção e educação para mudar comportamentos relacionados à violência de gênero, além de maior discussão do tema em escolas, empresas e espaços públicos.

Fabiano Contarato é natural de Nova Venécia, no Norte do Espírito Santo. Foi professor universitário e delegado da Polícia Civil por 27 anos. Em 2018, foi eleito senador da República em seu primeiro cargo eletivo.

O Bom Dia Espírito Santo iniciou nesta segunda-feira (21) uma série de entrevistas ao vivo com candidatos ao Senado.

Pelas regras definidas pela TV Gazeta , participam os candidatos que tiveram 5% ou mais na última pesquisa do Instituto Quaest contratada pela emissora e que estejam necessariamente entre os cinco primeiros colocados no levantamento.

A ordem das entrevistas segue a posição dos candidatos na pesquisa. Cada candidato tem 30 minutos de entrevista e mais um minuto para considerações finais. As entrevistas também são transmitidas ao vivo pelo g1 e pelo Globoplay.

Na segunda-feira (21), o entrevistado foi Renato Casagrande (PSB) , na terça foi Sérgio Meneguelli , nesta quarta-feira (23) foi com Fabiano Contarato (PT). Na quinta-feira (24), será a vez de Rose de Freitas (MDB), e, na sexta-feira (25), a entrevistada será Maguinha Malta.

articles.title: Nunes Marques manda Lula retirar vídeo sobre caso Master do ar | G1
articles.standfirst: No vídeo de um minuto e vinte segundos, o presidente Lula diz que o Brasil "não pode ficar refém de vazamentos seletivos" e defende um código de ética para o Judiciário. Flávio Bolsonaro é investigado pela Polícia Federal por envolvimento com Daniel Vorcaro.
articles.summary: Nunes Marques atende pedido de Flávio Bolsonaro e ordena remoção de vídeo de Lula sobre o caso Master.
articles.body:
Presidente Lula em vídeo de 3 de setembro sobre o caso Master — Foto: Reprodução

O ministro Kassio Nunes Marques, presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), determinou que o presidente Lula (PT) tire do ar um vídeo publicado em 3 de setembro em que trata do caso Master . A decisão se deu nesta terça-feira (22). Quem solicitou a retirada do ar do material foi Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência. Flávio é investigado pela Polícia Federal por envolvimento com o caso.

No vídeo de um minuto e vinte segundos, o presidente Lula diz que o Brasil "não pode ficar refém de vazamentos seletivos" e defende um código de ética para o Judiciário.

"O escândalo do Banco Master é o maior roubo da história do Brasil. Roubaram milhões de pessoas de muitos estados e municípios. O banqueiro, líder do esquema, tem relações com muita gente poderosa. E foi no meu governo que ele foi preso e seu banco fechado. Há suspeita de políticos e agentes públicos envolvidos. Nossa democracia não pode ficar refém de vazamentos seletivos", disse Lula no vídeo de 3 de setembro.

Na decisão dessa terça, Nunes Marques apontou que Lula usou em benefício da candidatura um prédio público e símbolos associados ao cargo de Presidência da República. A Lei das Eleições proíbe essa conduta para fazer campanha.

"A realização de manifestação de conteúdo eleitoral em cômodo da residência oficial não é, portanto, por si só, proibida. Sua licitude depende, contudo, do cumprimento cumulativo das condições estabelecidas pelo dispositivo, entre elas a utilização de ambiente neutro, desprovido de elementos associados ao poder público ou ao cargo ocupado", disse Nunes Marques na decisão.

"O vídeo foi gravado no Palácio da Alvorada e divulgado nas páginas do primeiro representado [Lula] indicadas à Justiça Eleitoral como canais oficiais de sua campanha à reeleição. As imagens juntadas aos autos mostram o primeiro representado [Lula] com a bandeira nacional ao fundo, estandarte de caráter institucional, além de outros elementos visuais associados ao exercício do cargo."

O presidente do TSE deu prazo de 24 horas para que o conteúdo seja removido das redes sociais de Lula. Às 8h45 dessa quarta-feira, o vídeo ainda estava no YouTube e no Instagram do presidente. Nunes Marques proibiu que o material seja usado na propaganda eleitoral gratuita.

O ministro estabeleceu prazo de cinco dias para que o governo federal informe ao TSE o registro de acesso, autorização de entrada e identificação funcional e civil da equipe técnica que participou da gravação, a identificação de servidores e equipamentos eventualmente empregados na produção e edição do material e a comprovação da origem do custeio do material.

O vídeo do início de setembro marcou a primeira declaração pública do presidente Lula sobre a crise no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).

Naquela semana, haviam vindo à tona mensagens enviadas pelo ex-banqueiro preso Daniel Vorcaro ao ministro do Supremo Alexandre de Moraes. Das conversas, emergiram suspeitas de que Vorcaro pedia conselhos jurídicos a Moraes e de que os dois eram próximos.

Moraes, no entanto, não é o único ministro que aparece em material proveniente do celular do ex-banqueiro. Foram citados nos documentos da investigação do Master André Mendonça, Dias Toffoli e Kassio Nunes Marques.

Nessa terça-feira (22), vieram à tona mensagens de Vorcaro e de auxiliares com referências a Nunes Marques . O ex-banqueiro teria bancado, por exemplo, hospedagem em hotel de luxo em São Paulo para o presidente do TSE.

articles.title: Majority of voters say country is on wrong track, favor Democrats in 2026: Poll
articles.summary: A new survey found that a majority of Americans believe the country is on the wrong track and that more Americans would vote for a Democratic candidate over a Republican candidate in the 2026 midterm elections. The survey, commissioned by the Bipartisan Policy Center (BPC) Action and American Policy Ventures and conducted by Cygnal and…
articles.body:
A new survey found that a majority of Americans believe the country is on the wrong track and that more Americans would vote for a Democratic candidate over a Republican candidate in the 2026 midterm elections.

The survey, commissioned by the Bipartisan Policy Center (BPC) Action and American Policy Ventures and conducted by Cygnal and Impact Research, was conducted among 1,500 likely general election voters between Sept. 1-2. It found that 60.5 percent of respondents believed that the country is mostly or definitely on the wrong track.

By contrast, only 36.2 percent of those surveyed said they believe the country is headed mostly or definitely in the right direction, and 3.3 percent of respondents were unsure.

The poll also found that 50.7 percent of respondents said they would probably or definitely vote for a Democratic candidate for U.S. Congress if the election were held today, compared with 42.1 percent who said they would probably or definitely vote for a Republican candidate. Another 7.2 percent were undecided.

The economy and affordability have emerged as central issues in the 2026 midterms, with voters frustrated over the rising gas prices, grocery costs and inflation amid the Iran war.

The poll found that 66.6 percent of respondents believe that given what they pay in taxes, the government is doing somewhat too little or way too little in helping Americans who raise families. Only 14.7 percent believe the government is doing the right amount, while 10.5 percent of respondents say the government is doing somewhat or way too much.

Meanwhile, respondents said the issues that cause them the most stress are healthcare and insurance costs, groceries and food and rent or mortgage, according to the survey. The poll found that parents raising kids said they feel the pressure more in housing, while elderly and disability caregivers feel it most in healthcare.

“Too often, Members of Congress face political backlash for working across the aisle,” Liam deClive-Lowe, president of American Policy Ventures, said in a press release. “But this poll shows that policies to support families have widespread backing across the political spectrum. The lawmakers who are leading on these issues have an opportunity to help break through the rising tide of polarization through concrete policy results that help American families.”

Michele Stockwell, president of BPC Action, echoed those sentiments, arguing in a statement that the “poll underscores an important point for Washington: the cost of raising a family is not a partisan issue.”

“Two-thirds of voters say the federal government is doing too little, and majorities of Republicans, Independents, and Democrats want solutions. That is a mandate to act,” Stockwell said.
